tools.name: structuredDiff
tools.description: Compare two JSON values or two texts without AI. Use this to see exactly what changed between two supplied versions. format json (default): returns added, removed, and changed paths as JSON Pointers; objects compare by key (order ignored), arrays by index (no move detection), and a different type co

tools.name: validateJsonSchema
tools.description: Validate JSON against a JSON Schema without AI. Use this to check supplied data against a supplied JSON Schema before relying on it. Returns valid, and each failure with the JSON Pointer of the failing value, the schema path, the keyword, and the reason. Nothing is repaired or coerced. Drafts 2020-1

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: readSource, checkQuote, checkCitations, validateJsonSchema, search, fetch, submitFeedback · Private data: fetch, submitFeedback · Public sink: readSource, checkQuote, checkCitations, structuredDiff, validateJsonSchema, inspectAgentAccess, submitFeedback · Destructive: readSource, structuredDiff, inspectAgentAccess.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: readSource, checkQuote, checkCitations, validateJsonSchema, search, fetch, submitFeedback · Private data: fetch, submitFeedback · Public sink: readSource, checkQuote, checkCitations, structuredDiff, validateJsonSchema, inspectAgentAccess, submitFeedback · Destructive: readSource, structuredDiff, inspectAgentAccess

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
